lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Childless Hannah prays at Shiloh and vows to give a son to the LORD; Eli blesses her, Samuel is born, and after he is weaned she brings him to serve the LORD at Shiloh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Hannah prayed for a child and what she did when God gave Samuel?
ev: Retell what Hannah asked and vowed (1:10-11)
Say what Hannah did when Samuel was weaned (1:24-28)

nodes.d: 1 Samuel runs from the birth of Samuel to Saul's death on Mount Gilboa: Samuel as prophet and judge, Israel's request for a king, Saul's reign and rejection, and David's rise and flight from Saul.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Samuel from Hannah's prayer to the death of Saul?
ev: Name the three main figures: Samuel, Saul and David
Say how the book begins and ends (1:1-20, 31:1-13)

nodes.d: Hannah praises the LORD as holy and a rock, who kills and makes alive, brings low and lifts up, raises the poor and breaks his adversaries, and gives strength to his king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Hannah's song teaches about the LORD?
ev: Say what Hannah says about the LORD (2:2)
Name some reversals she describes (2:4-8)
Say what she says about the LORD's king and anointed (2:10)

nodes.t: Eli's wicked sons and the word against his house
nodes.d: Hophni and Phinehas abuse the sacrifices and the women at the tabernacle while Samuel grows in favour; a man of God tells Eli that the LORD will cut off his house, and that both sons will die in one day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why God judged Eli's house?
ev: Say what Eli's sons did wrong (2:12-17, 2:22)
Say what sign was given to Eli (2:34)
Say what the LORD promises about a faithful priest (2:35)

nodes.d: The LORD calls the boy Samuel three times before Eli tells him how to answer; the LORD tells him he will judge Eli's house, Samuel tells Eli everything, and all Israel knows he is a prophet.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God called Samuel in the night?
ev: Retell how Samuel heard the LORD
Say what Samuel said when he finally answered (3:10)
Say what the LORD told Samuel and how Eli responded (3:11-18)

nodes.t: The ark is captured and Eli dies
nodes.d: Israel is defeated by the Philistines, brings the ark of the covenant from Shiloh to the camp, loses it as Hophni and Phinehas are killed, and Eli dies on hearing the news; Phinehas' wife names her son Ichabod.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the ark was lost and what happened to Eli?
ev: Say why Israel fetched the ark and what happened (4:3-11)
Say what happened to Eli and his sons (4:11-18)
Say what Ichabod means in the text (4:21-22)

nodes.d: The Philistines set the ark beside Dagon in Ashdod, where Dagon falls before it; the LORD's hand strikes Ashdod, Gath and Ekron, and they want the ark sent away.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the Philistines kept the ark?
ev: Say what happened to Dagon (5:3-4)
Say what happened to the people of the cities that held the ark (5:6-12)

nodes.t: The ark comes back to Israel
nodes.d: The Philistines send the ark home on a cart pulled by two cows with a trespass offering; the cows go straight to Beth-shemesh, where seventy men are struck for looking into the ark, and the ark is taken to Kirjath-jearim.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the ark went back to Israel?
ev: Say what the Philistines sent with the ark (6:4-8)
Say what the cows did (6:12)
Say what happened at Beth-shemesh (6:19-21)

nodes.d: After twenty years, Samuel calls Israel to put away foreign gods; at Mizpeh they fast and confess, the LORD thunders on the Philistines, and Samuel sets up the stone Ebenezer, saying the LORD has helped them so far.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Mizpeh and why Samuel set up the stone Ebenezer?
ev: Say what Samuel told Israel to do (7:3)
Explain what Ebenezer means (7:12)
Say how Samuel judged Israel (7:15-17)

nodes.d: Samuel's sons take bribes, and the elders ask for a king like the nations; the LORD tells Samuel that they have rejected him, and Samuel warns what a king will take, but the people insist.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Israel asked for a king and what the LORD said about it?
ev: Say why the elders asked for a king (8:4-5, 8:19-20)
Say what the LORD said the request meant (8:7-8)
List things Samuel said a king would take (8:11-17)

nodes.t: Saul seeks his father's donkeys and meets Samuel
nodes.d: Saul searches for lost donkeys, goes with his servant to the seer Samuel, whom the LORD had told the day before that he would send a man to be captain over Israel; Samuel hosts him at a meal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Saul came to meet Samuel?
ev: Say what Saul went to find
Say what the LORD told Samuel about Saul (9:15-17)

nodes.d: Samuel pours oil on Saul as captain over the LORD's inheritance, gives him three signs, and God gives him another heart; Saul prophesies among the prophets but tells his uncle nothing of the kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Samuel anointed Saul?
ev: Say what Samuel did to Saul (10:1)
Name the signs that came to pass (10:2-10)
Say the proverb that arose (10:11-12)

nodes.d: Samuel gathers Israel at Mizpeh, reminds them they rejected God by asking for a king, and Saul is chosen by lot, found hiding among the baggage, and acclaimed; some worthless men despise him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Saul was chosen as king in front of all the people?
ev: Say how Saul was chosen (10:20-21)
Say where Saul was found and what the people shouted (10:22-24)

nodes.d: Nahash the Ammonite threatens Jabesh-gilead; the Spirit of God comes on Saul, who summons Israel, defeats the Ammonites, spares those who had despised him, and is confirmed as king at Gilgal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Saul saved Jabesh-gilead and what he said afterward?
ev: Say what Nahash demanded (11:2)
Say how Saul answered the call to spare his opponents (11:12-13)
Say who gets the credit Saul gives (11:13)

nodes.d: Samuel asks Israel to witness his honesty, recounts the LORD's righteous acts, says their request for a king was wrong, sends thunder and rain, and tells them to fear the LORD, promising not to stop praying for them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Samuel's farewell speech and the warning at its end?
ev: Say what Samuel asked the people to testify (12:3-5)
Say what sign confirmed his words (12:16-18)
Say what Samuel promised and what he told them to do (12:20-25)

nodes.d: Facing the Philistines, Saul waits seven days for Samuel, then offers the burnt offering himself; Samuel says he acted foolishly and his kingdom will not continue, because the LORD has sought a man after his own heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Saul did wrong at Gilgal?
ev: Say what Saul did and why (13:8-12)
Say what Samuel said would happen (13:13-14)

nodes.t: Jonathan's victory and Saul's rash oath
nodes.d: Jonathan and his armour-bearer attack a Philistine garrison, saying the LORD may work for them, and the Philistines panic; Saul's oath forbidding food nearly costs Jonathan his life until the people rescue him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jonathan did and what Saul's oath caused?
ev: Say what Jonathan said about the LORD saving by many or by few (14:6)
Explain Saul's oath and what Jonathan did (14:24-27)
Say how Jonathan was spared (14:43-45)

nodes.d: Samuel tells Saul to destroy Amalek; Saul spares King Agag and the best livestock, Samuel says obedience is better than sacrifice and that the LORD has rejected Saul as king, and the LORD repents of making Saul king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD rejected Saul as king?
ev: Say what the LORD commanded and what Saul did instead (15:3, 15:9)
Say what Samuel said about obedience and sacrifice (15:22-23)
Say what Samuel did to Agag (15:32-33)

nodes.d: The LORD sends Samuel to Jesse of Bethlehem to anoint a new king; passing over the older sons because the LORD looks on the heart, Samuel anoints the youngest, David, and the Spirit comes on him while the Spirit leaves Saul.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David was chosen and anointed?
ev: Say whom Samuel was sent to and why (16:1-3)
Say what the LORD said about outward appearance and the heart (16:7)
Say who was anointed and what followed (16:12-13)

nodes.d: An evil spirit from the LORD troubles Saul after the Spirit departs from him, and his servants bring David, who plays the harp, to ease him; Saul loves David and makes him his armour-bearer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why David came to serve Saul?
ev: Say why David was brought to Saul
Say what happened when David played (16:23)

nodes.d: Goliath of Gath defies Israel for forty days; David, sent with food for his brothers, volunteers, refuses Saul's armour, and in the name of the LORD of hosts kills Goliath with a sling and stone, saying the battle is the LORD's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of David and Goliath and who David trusted?
ev: Retell how David came to fight Goliath
Say what David told Goliath about the LORD (17:45-47)
Say how David killed Goliath (17:48-51)

nodes.d: After Goliath, Jonathan loves David and makes a covenant with him; the women's song makes Saul jealous, and he hurls a javelin at David and sets him dangerous tasks, but sees that the LORD is with David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Saul grew jealous of David?
ev: Say what Jonathan gave David (18:3-4)
Say what the women sang and how Saul reacted (18:6-9)
Say why Saul was afraid of David (18:12, 18:28-29)

nodes.d: Saul orders David killed; Jonathan pleads for him and Saul swears an oath, but then throws his javelin again, Michal helps David escape through a window, and Saul himself prophesies when he follows David to Samuel at Ramah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David escaped from Saul?
ev: Say how Jonathan and Michal each helped David
Say what happened to Saul's messengers and to Saul at Naioth (19:20-24)

nodes.d: David asks Jonathan to find out Saul's intent; Saul's anger at the new moon feast confirms he wants David dead, and Jonathan signals this with arrows, before the friends part in tears after renewing their oath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jonathan warned David with the arrows?
ev: Say how Jonathan and David planned to learn Saul's mind (20:5-23)
Say what Saul did to Jonathan at the feast (20:30-34)
Say what the two friends swore at parting (20:42)

nodes.d: David gets the holy bread and Goliath's sword from Ahimelech the priest at Nob, where Doeg the Edomite sees him, then flees to Achish king of Gath and pretends to be mad.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what David did at Nob and at Gath?
ev: Say what David received at Nob (21:6, 21:9)
Say who saw David there (21:7)
Say how David escaped from Gath (21:13-15)

nodes.t: Doeg kills the priests of Nob
nodes.d: David gathers distressed men at the cave of Adullam; Saul, told by Doeg that Ahimelech helped David, has Doeg kill the priests of Nob, and Abiathar escapes to David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened to the priests at Nob?
ev: Say who joined David at Adullam (22:1-2)
Say what Doeg did and who escaped (22:18-20)

nodes.t: David saves Keilah and is hunted in the wilderness
nodes.d: David asks the LORD before rescuing Keilah and again about Saul, leaves before Saul arrives, and is pursued in the wilderness of Ziph and Maon until a Philistine raid recalls Saul; Jonathan strengthens David and they make a covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David escaped Saul in the wilderness and what he asked of the LORD?
ev: Say how David sought guidance from the LORD (23:2, 23:9-12)
Say what Jonathan told David (23:16-18)
Say how David escaped at Maon (23:26-28)

nodes.t: David spares Saul in the cave
nodes.d: Saul enters the cave at Engedi where David and his men are hiding; David cuts off a corner of Saul's robe but refuses to harm the LORD's anointed, and Saul weeps and acknowledges David will be king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why David would not harm Saul?
ev: Say what David did and did not do in the cave (24:4-7)
Say what David told Saul afterward (24:9-15)
Say what Saul admitted (24:17-20)

nodes.d: Nabal insults David's men who had protected his flocks; David sets out to kill his household, but Abigail brings food and speaks to him, David is restrained from bloodshed, the LORD strikes Nabal dead, and Abigail becomes David's wife.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Abigail kept David from shedding blood?
ev: Say how Nabal treated David's men (25:10-11)
Say what Abigail did and what David said to her (25:18-33)
Say what happened to Nabal (25:36-38)

nodes.t: David spares Saul a second time
nodes.d: At Hachilah David and Abishai enter Saul's sleeping camp; David refuses Abishai's offer to kill Saul, takes his spear and water jar, and calls from a distance, and Saul admits he has sinned.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when David found Saul sleeping at Hachilah?
ev: Say what David and Abishai found in Saul's camp (26:7)
Say why David would not let Abishai strike (26:9-11)
Say what David took and what Saul said (26:12, 26:21)

nodes.t: David among the Philistines at Ziklag
nodes.d: Fearing Saul, David goes with his six hundred men to Achish of Gath, is given Ziklag, and raids peoples in the south while making Achish think he is raiding Judah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why David went to live among the Philistines?
ev: Say why David went to Gath (27:1)
Say what Achish gave David and what David told Achish about his raids (27:6-12)

nodes.t: Saul and the medium at Endor
nodes.d: With the Philistines camped against him, Saul gets no answer from the LORD and consults a medium at Endor, despite having banned them; the figure of Samuel tells him that the LORD has become his enemy and that he and his sons will die the next day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why going to the medium at Endor was wrong for Saul and what he was told?
ev: Say why Saul went to the woman at Endor (28:5-7)
Say what Samuel told Saul (28:16-19)

nodes.t: The Philistine lords send David back
nodes.d: The Philistine lords refuse to let David fight with them against Israel, so Achish sends David and his men back from Aphek.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why David did not fight with the Philistines against Israel?
ev: Say why the Philistine lords objected to David (29:3-5)
Say what Achish told David to do (29:7-11)

nodes.t: David recovers what was taken at Ziklag
nodes.d: Amalekites burn Ziklag and take the families captive; David strengthens himself in the LORD, inquires through the ephod, pursues and recovers everyone and everything, and rules that those who stayed behind share equally in the spoil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David got back the families taken from Ziklag?
ev: Say what David found at Ziklag and what he did first (30:3-8)
Say what David ruled about the spoil (30:23-25)

nodes.t: The death of Saul and his sons
nodes.d: Israel flees before the Philistines at Mount Gilboa; Jonathan and two brothers are killed, Saul takes his own life after being wounded, and the men of Jabesh-gilead recover and bury the bodies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Saul and Jonathan died?
ev: Say who died at Gilboa
Say what the men of Jabesh-gilead did (31:11-13)

nodes.d: Judges tells of Israel after Joshua's death, repeatedly falling into idolatry, being oppressed, crying out and being delivered by judges, and ends with the refrain that there was no king in Israel and everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the cycle of sin, oppression, crying out and deliverance in Judges?
ev: Describe the repeating pattern in Judges 2:11-19
Name several judges and the enemies they faced
Say what 21:25 says about Israel at the end

nodes.d: 2 Samuel follows David from the news of Saul's death to his kingship over Judah and then all Israel, the LORD's promise of a lasting house, his sin with Bathsheba and its consequences in his own family, Absalom's and Sheba's revolts, and closing songs, warriors and a census.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 2 Samuel from David's lament for Saul to the census at the end?
ev: Say how the book begins and what David did first
Name the promise in chapter 7
Name some consequences in David's family after chapter 11

nodes.t: David hears of Saul's death and laments
nodes.d: An Amalekite brings David news of Saul's death and claims to have killed him; David has him put to death for slaying the LORD's anointed, and composes a lament for Saul and Jonathan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David responded to the news that Saul was dead?
ev: Say what the Amalekite claimed and what David did (1:8-16)
Say what David said about Jonathan in his lament (1:26)

nodes.t: David brings the ark to Jerusalem
nodes.d: Uzzah dies when he touches the ark on the cart, so David leaves it at Obed-edom's house; after three months he brings it into the city with sacrifices and dancing, and Michal despises him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the ark came to Jerusalem?
ev: Say what happened to Uzzah (6:6-7)
Say what happened to Obed-edom's house (6:11)
Say how David and Michal reacted when the ark came in (6:14-16, 6:20-23)

nodes.d: David asks if any of Saul's house remains to whom he can show kindness for Jonathan's sake, learns from Ziba of Mephibosheth, restores Saul's land to him, and has him eat at the king's table.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David was kind to Mephibosheth and why?
ev: Say why David sought someone from Saul's house (9:1)
Say what David gave Mephibosheth (9:7, 9:10-13)

nodes.d: Several descendants of the giant, including a brother of Goliath, are slain in battles at Gob and Gath by David's men after David grows faint.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of David's men who defeated the Philistine giants?
ev: Say who rescued David when he grew faint (21:15-17)
Say who killed the brother of Goliath (21:19)

nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.d: Pharisees object that the disciples pluck grain on the sabbath; Jesus cites David eating the shewbread and the priests in the temple, and says the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus said about David and the sabbath?
ev: Explain the Pharisees’ objection
Say what examples Jesus gave

nodes.d: The gospel of Mark, from “the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God” (1:1) through Jesus’ ministry in Galilee, the road to Jerusalem and his death, to the empty tomb and commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Mark is about and where it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: John and the start of ministry (1), Galilee (1-8), the way to Jerusalem (8-10), the last week and passion (11-15), the empty tomb (16)
Say what Mark calls the book in 1:1

nodes.t: Lord of the sabbath: the grainfield
nodes.d: When disciples pluck grain on the sabbath, Jesus cites David eating the shewbread and says the sabbath was made for man and the Son of man is Lord of it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about the sabbath?
ev: State the objection and Jesus’ example
Explain “the sabbath was made for man”
